caption: Notes: the twelve notes as twelve keys across the matrix, each lit as strongly as it sounds; the colour follows the chord
why: Bands tell you how loud the bass and treble are; they do not tell you what is being played. Notes does: it measures the twelve pitch classes - C, C#, D up to B, in any octave - so you can see the chord, and colour an effect by it.

`note` is the strongest note as a position round the circle of notes - into a hue, each chord gets its own colour - and `clarity` says how clearly it stands out. It reads the studio's audioreactive patch (the sim's synth plays chords); WLED's stock audioreactive does not have it. Its neighbours: Spectrum shows the bands; Timbre the brightness of the mix; Notes the harmony.
steps: **index** is unwired, so it is the pixel's own `u`: the twelve notes are spread across the matrix, C at the left, B at the right.

`level` is how strongly that note is sounding: a level meter: the level plus **Coords** `v` reaches 1 (a **Threshold**) only where `v` is above 1 minus the level, so a column is lit from the bottom as high as the level, in the **Palette**'s colours across.
**smooth** is 0.5: how much the levels are smoothed from frame to frame.
`note` (the strongest) is the **Palette**'s index for every key, so the whole picture takes the colour of the chord, changing as the synth's chords change. The trace shows `note` and `clarity`.

try.label: Steadier
try.text: smooth 0.9: the keys rise and fall slowly - the chord rather than every note.

try.label: Raw
try.text: smooth 0: every frame's measurement as it is - jumpy, but quick to follow.
